analysis.title: GS Crook - GS MORNING: 1) CPI Review, 2) Korea Update, 3) Credit Concerns & AI, 4) Risks Around Higher Bond Yields and 5) 5 Key Charts 15 Oct 2026
key_insights: September CPI was above expectations: headline +0.65% m/m (GS +0.59%, median forecast +0.6%, prior +0.40%), core +0.33% m/m (GS +0.24%, median +0.2%, prior +0.29%). Year over year, headline was +3.74% and core +2.56%.

GS US economics attributes the core upside partly to shelter. OER rose 0.35% m/m and added about 5bp more to core than GS expected. OER strength was concentrated in the Midwest (+0.68%, SA by GS). Travel services, autos and recreation goods were also firm.

From the CPI details, GS estimates September core PCE rose 0.32% m/m, versus 0.20% expected before the CPI release. That corresponds to +3.09% y/y. The revision reflects upside surprises in OER, hotels and recreation forecasts.

GS FX strategy (Jenkins) notes that front-end rate pricing did a round trip after yesterday's data, partly because of equity weakness and partly because of prior Fed speaker guidance. Next catalysts are PPI, which will help finalize the core PCE tracking number against GS's 32bp, and Warsh's speech on Friday at 04:30 London time.

KOSPI fell for a 7th straight session, its longest losing streak since September 2024, with a peak-to-trough drawdown of roughly 20%. In the past 20 years only March 2020 (-20.5%) and August 2011 (-15.1%) matched a multi-day sell-off of this size without a relief day.

GS Asia equity sales trading ties the KOSPI sell-off to the removal of the corporate bid. Samsung Electronics completed its buyback program on October 6 and SK Hynix is tapering. Foreign institutional selling, about 80-87% concentrated in the two chip heavyweights, has met an empty domestic bid, broken key psychological levels and triggered forced margin liquidations.

GS APAC equity strategy (Moe) keeps a 12-month KOSPI target of 12,000 and sees a favourable risk/reward. It cites a long AI hardware cycle and market earnings growth forecasts of 320%, 35% and 20% for 2026-2028. Valuation is low: forward P/E 5.1x (-2.7 s.d.), price to cash flow 4.7x, trailing P/B 1.8x versus 26% forward 24-month ROE.

GS flags three monitorable risks to the Korea case, not base-case drags: durability of the memory cycle, retail leverage and leveraged-ETF overhangs, and competition from Chinese open-weight AI models plus hyperscaler capex funding.

GS EM strategy (Sun Lu) reads BOK governor Shin's comments, that further KRW gains would be desirable and policy stays restrictive until inflation converges, as a sign that 1300 is likely not a line in the sand for USDKRW. Samsung and Hynix need to convert 70-80% of their trade surplus to meet local KRW payments, which lowers USDKRW's gravity. Key dates: Oct 27 (Hynix results) and Nov 18-20 (Samsung 40tn dividend payment).

Privorotsky (GS equity trading) says credit concerns have entered the AI spending equilibrium and the market is reading them as a growth shock. The GS global neocloud basket is down 20% in five sessions, about a 1st percentile move over ten years, and hyperscaler IG spreads widened another 7.4bp last week.

Privorotsky does not see a demand crisis: aggregate token consumption continues to surprise to the upside. The open risks are financing and physical delivery (power, data center energization, gigawatts), constraints that become more tangible in 2027 and 2028. He sees the effect on leveraged middlemen and neoclouds, and an advantage for powered capacity and strong balance sheets.

Privorotsky argues much bad news is priced. Neoclouds had a historic liquidation, while quality rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83. Discretionary net positioning is low and rates are rallying, and his gut is that pockets have overreacted. Stabilizing lower rates would improve the financing equation.

Allison Nathan's piece notes global bond yields at multi-decade highs with resilient growth. The IMF's Adrian is relatively sanguine, GS economists expect a modest growth drag that grows if yields stay at or above current levels, and Moody's Zandi calls the US economy vulnerable and sees one-in-three odds of it going off the rails. The key watch item is whether the leveraged, interconnected AI investment boom can withstand higher rates.

GS equity strategy (Snider): the S&P 500 is on pace for a fourth straight year of double-digit returns despite long-term Treasury yields at multi-decade highs. Current yield levels should not prevent further gains, but a further sharp rise would pressure the rally.

GS credit strategy (Lynam): credit spreads are under 15% of the USD IG index all-in yield, versus an average of 45% in 2019-2021. This makes parts of corporate credit a quasi-rates product, and rising rate volatility could turn rates from a tailwind into a headwind for credit through lower investor demand and weaker corporate fundamentals.

Charts flagged: China's September trade surplus hit a record US$133.5bn, 3-month implied correlation is below the 2nd percentile of the last 20 years, and Australia's September unemployment rate rose to 4.7%, weaker than expected.

sector_views.rationale: GS keeps a 12m KOSPI target of 12,000, citing a long AI hardware cycle, rapid earnings growth and very low valuations, despite the near-term sell-off.
Credit and financing concerns hit leveraged neoclouds, while demand holds up. Powered capacity and strong balance sheets are favored over leveraged middlemen.

earnings_insights: GS Asia strategy forecasts Korean aggregate market earnings growth of 320% for 2026, 35% for 2027 and 20% for 2028 (GS forecasts, not reported figures).
Upcoming: SK Hynix reports results on Oct 27. Samsung's 40tn dividend payment date falls on Nov 18-20.

risk_factors: Further sharp rise in Treasury yields or rate volatility could pressure the equity rally and credit.
Credit spreads widening in the AI vertical (hyperscaler IG spreads +7.4bp last week) could slow chip consumption, capex and growth.
Physical delivery constraints (power, data center energization, permitting) for AI buildout in 2027 and 2028.
Korea: durability of the memory cycle, retail leverage and leveraged-ETF overhangs, Chinese open-weight AI competition and hyperscaler capex funding.
Higher yields near-term hit US refinancing sooner than longer-duration issuers such as the UK (debt maturity profile chart).
Zandi sees one-in-three odds the US economy goes off the rails.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots KOSPI and USDKRW (source Marquee MarketView), with no values given in the text.
Chart 2 shows % of debt maturing within each timeframe by country, with the US facing refinancing sooner than longer-duration issuers such as the UK.
Chart 3 deconstructs the Bloomberg USD IG Corporate Index all-in yield into spread and risk-free components, with spreads under 15% as of September 28, 2026.
Chart 4: 3-month implied correlation is below the 2nd percentile over the last 20 years.
Chart 5: Australia unemployment rate rose to 4.7% in September, weaker than expected.
vol_and_positioning: 3-month implied correlation is below the 2nd percentile of the last 20 years (GS FICC & Equities chart).
Quality stocks rallied in 16 of 18 sessions with RSI at 83. Discretionary net positioning is low (Privorotsky).
The GS global neocloud basket fell 20% in five sessions, about a 1st percentile move over ten years.
KOSPI retail leverage and leveraged-ETF overhangs are flagged as monitorable risks. Forced margin liquidations accompanied the KOSPI break.
Rate volatility is increasing, which GS credit strategy monitors as a risk to credit demand and fundamentals.
geopolitical: China's trade surplus rose to a record US$133.5bn in September, per China Customs data in the chart section.
Political backdrop is cited as making data center logistics, permitting and policy messier into 2027 and 2028.

tension_points.bull_case: Aggregate token consumption keeps surprising upward, quality has rallied, positioning is light and rates are rallying. Privorotsky thinks pockets have overreacted and the structural thesis can survive.
tension_points.bear_case: Credit widening across the AI vertical is a warning. Neoclouds are down 20% in five sessions, hyperscaler IG spreads widened 7.4bp, and capital to finance compute may not keep up with demand.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further credit spread widening, or rates failing to stabilize lower, would undercut the recalibration view.

tension_points.bull_case: GS strategists say current yield levels should not stop the S&P 500 from rising, and the IMF's Adrian is relatively sanguine.
tension_points.bear_case: Zandi calls the economy vulnerable with one-in-three odds of going off the rails, and a further sharp rise in yields or rate volatility could pressure risk assets.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further sharp rise in yields or rate volatility from current levels.

tension_points.bull_case: GS keeps a 12,000 12m KOSPI target on rapid earnings growth, very low valuations and a long AI hardware cycle.
tension_points.bear_case: The removal of the corporate bid, forced margin liquidations and foreign selling concentrated in Samsung and SK Hynix drove a roughly 20% drawdown.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Weakening of the memory cycle, retail leverage and leveraged-ETF overhangs, or Chinese open-weight AI competition and hyperscaler capex funding problems.
